quizName: React Modules, JSX, Components, and Props

questions.question: What does `import` do in JavaScript modules?
options: It sends a file to the server
It brings in code that was exported from another file
It automatically creates a React component
It turns JSX into HTML
questions.explanation: `import` lets one file use values, functions, or components that were exported from another module.

questions.question: What does `export` do in a JavaScript module?
options: It deletes a variable after the file runs
It converts JSX into plain text
It makes a value available for other files to import
It only works inside `App.jsx`
questions.explanation: `export` marks something so other files can import and use it.

questions.question: What is special about `export default`?
options: It means the exported value cannot be imported anywhere else
It means the file is only for CSS
It automatically runs the function when the file loads
A file can have only one default export, and importers can choose its local name
questions.explanation: A module can have one default export. When importing it, you do not use curly braces and you can choose the local name.

options: `import { Button } from './Button';`
`import Button from './Button';`
`import default Button from './Button';`
`import './Button' as Button;`
questions.explanation: Default exports are imported without curly braces, so `import Button from './Button';` is correct.

options: `import { add } from './math';`
`import add from './math';`
`import math.add from './math';`
`import * add from './math';`
questions.explanation: Named exports are imported with curly braces, so `import { add } from './math';` is correct.

questions.question: What is JSX?
options: A database used by React
A browser feature that replaces CSS
A syntax extension that lets us write HTML-like markup inside JavaScript
A special file type that cannot include JavaScript
questions.explanation: JSX lets us write UI markup in a way that looks similar to HTML while still working inside JavaScript.

options: A paragraph with the text Hello world
A heading element with the text Hello world
Nothing, because components cannot return JSX
An error, because `return` is not allowed in a function
questions.explanation: The component returns JSX for an `h1`, so it renders a heading that says `Hello world`.

questions.question: Why do React component names usually start with a capital letter?
options: Because lowercase component names automatically run faster
Because JavaScript requires all functions to start with capital letters
Because JSX does not allow lowercase letters
Because React uses capitalization to distinguish custom components from built-in HTML tags
questions.explanation: React treats uppercase names like `Greeting` as components and lowercase names like `div` as built-in HTML elements.

questions.question: What are props in React?
options: Inputs passed from a parent component to a child component
Special loops used inside JSX
CSS files attached to a component
Errors created by missing imports
questions.explanation: Props are values passed into a component so it can display or use data from its parent.

options: `Hello undefined`
`Hello Ada`
`name="Ada"`
Nothing, because props cannot be used inside JSX
questions.explanation: The component destructures the `name` prop from the props object. Since the component is rendered with `name="Ada"`, the page shows `Hello Ada`.

options: Nothing is wrong
The component must be exported first
The component is returning two sibling JSX elements without wrapping them in one parent element
The `p` tag is not allowed in React
questions.explanation: A component must return one parent JSX element. The `h2` and `p` should be wrapped in a `div` or fragment.

options: No error
`src` is not allowed in JSX
Images can only be used inside CSS
React requires `img` to be written with a closing slash, like ``
questions.explanation: In JSX, self-closing tags such as `img` should be written with `/>`.

options: `User: sam`
`User: {username}`
`Profile sam`
Nothing, because destructuring props is not allowed
questions.explanation: The component destructures the `username` prop directly from the props object. Since `username="sam"` is passed in, the page renders `User: sam`.

options: An `h1` containing `Welcome`
Nothing, because `title` was not passed in
An error, because default values are not allowed in component parameters
An `h1` containing `undefined`
questions.explanation: Because the `title` prop has a default value of `'Welcome'`, the component can still render that text even when no `title` prop is passed.

options: Nothing is wrong
Default exports cannot be functions
React will treat `greeting` like a built-in HTML tag because it starts with a lowercase letter
JSX cannot render headings
questions.explanation: In JSX, lowercase names are treated like HTML tags. React components should start with a capital letter, such as `Greeting`.

options: Nothing is wrong; the page will show `Hello Ada`
The `Greeting` component must use `export default` to receive props
React components cannot be nested inside other components
The prop name does not match. The component expects `name`, but `App` passes `username`
questions.explanation: The `Greeting` component expects a prop called `name`, but `App` passes `username`. Because the prop names do not match, `name` will be `undefined` unless the component provides a default value.
